sourceFacts.fact: In a seriously unwell child with suspected meningitis or sepsis, urgent antibiotics take priority over performing LP.
LP requires a neurological examination and consideration of contraindications; obtain CSF when it is safe and appropriate.

expectedLabels: Do not delay antibiotics for LP
layoutSpecification: Title 'Suspected meningitis: protect treatment time'. LEFT one plain hospital assessment card labelled 'Seriously unwell child'. From it branch into TWO parallel lanes extending to RIGHT. UPPER lane a THICK uninterrupted teal arrow goes directly to an unmeasured plain medicine vial and clock labelled 'Urgent antibiotics'. LOWER lane a thinner ochre arrow leads first to a shield/checklist labelled 'Assess LP safety', then a small arrow labelled 'When safe' to a closed clear-fluid specimen tube labelled 'CSF sample when safe'. Absolutely no arrow from the LP/checklist lane into the antibiotics lane and no stopbar on antibiotics. Bottom 'Do not delay antibiotics for LP'. No needle, patient back, spine, brain, dose, fixed number of minutes or clinical LP instructions. This shows parallel priorities and a safety-dependent diagnostic step.
forbiddenAnatomy: No internal organ, eye, ear, brain, tissue or bone anatomy
No diagnostic image, patient-specific lesion appearance or literal anatomical pathway

validation.pixelChecks: Pixel/structure check: thick upper arrow goes directly from seriously unwell child to urgent antibiotics; independent lower lane reaches LP safety assessment before safety-qualified CSF sampling. No prerequisite connection from LP to antibiotics; no time/dose number. Renderer added clinical status, bleeding risk and other factors inside checklist; these broad domains are consistent with RCH safety assessment and are not presented as an exhaustive procedure checklist. No internal anatomy or needle placement.
